en: I thought you might be the new factory manager.
You look like such a fine gentleman.
Hello. I'm Kürten.
Do you remember me?
I remember you very well.
I mean, you don't often see someone
dressed the way you are...
Ahh... What should I do...
, please hear me out.
The truth is, there's someone I'm in love with.
She's a woman I always see in Alster Park,
and she is ever so beautiful...
If you love her that much, why not tell her?
Would she even look at someone like me?
note: Shared by 99395 and 100056 (in 100056 it follows 'Hmmm. But...', so no leading 'But').

en: , I finally worked up my courage
and spoke to the woman in Alster Park.
But it was no good, just as I feared...
She's waiting there for her lover to return,
or so I'm told.
Oh, I just want to die.
There is no need to die over it.
Come now, I'm sure you will soon
find yourself a new love.
Do you think so?
It's strange, but when you say so, I start
to feel that it might be true.
For now, I'll think a little longer about
whether to live or die...
Thank you!
Thanks to you, I've found a new love.
She works at the same factory, and she's
note: Shared by 99506 (+#2591) and 100180 (+#2649, slice 033): the next row must continue 'and she's ...'.

en: the sweetest-natured girl...
It's because you told me not to die back then
that I've been able to find such happiness.
I mean it,
note: 'I mean it, ' + NAME + #2595 '.' / then #2557 'It's all thanks to you.' (99506) or #2599 (99572).
'.' as agreed with slice 031 (#2557). Also used by Kröger msgs 132468 (after #3374) and 133325 (after #3433): those rows must end so NAME + '.' closes a sentence.

en: But now I have a new worry.
Whether or not I should marry her...
note: Shared by 99506 and 100180 (followed by #2655 'That's my new worry'-type line).

en: A happy sort of problem to have, isn't it?
I owe it all to you.
Whether I should marry her or not... I think
I'll keep agonizing over that for a while.
Is there something you want with me?
Haah... Factory work is so rough...
You must have come to the wrong house.
I mean,
note: No used_in; assumed to precede #2606 in msg 99784 (after #2604).

en: I can't imagine anyone having business with me.
No, that's not it. Um, well
note: No used_in; assumed [PLAYER] line followed by #180 '...' in msg 99824, so no final punctuation ('Um, well...').

en: If you don't mind, would you be my friend?
Huh? Really?
If you'll have me, I'd love to be your friend.
I'd love to be friends with you.
about my troubles!
note: Continues #2552 'You came all the way to my house to hear' (slice 031), like #2553.

en: I knew it, you're my true friend!
Now that I have a friend, should I give up
on having a sweetheart?
I found my sweetheart thanks to your advice.
Someone to love who loves me, and a friend...
How happy I am!
And you are...?
Nice to meet you.
Did you need something here at the factory?
No, not really... Um,
what if I said I'd like you to be my friend?
note: Also appears as a speaker-less prefix in msgs 87322, 99098, 119578, 165146, 221978; looks like an extraction artifact, translated for 99944 only.

en: Would that be all right?
Huh? Friends with me, of all people!?
W-Why, I'd be delighted.
I'm so happy.
From today on, you're my true friend.
Ah, my friend.
Thanks for listening to my troubles.
, listen to this.
The truth is, there's someone I like.
and she's really, really pretty...
If you like her that much, why not just tell her?
Hmmm. But...
, I finally worked up my nerve
But yeah, it was no good...
She's waiting there for her sweetheart
to come back, apparently.
